title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: October 2024
summary: October was a busy month for all CIG staff, with patch launches, Pyro in the PTU, and (of course) CitizenCon 2954. Alongside these major events, progress on upcoming features continued, with many teams finalizing content for Alpha 4.0 and 2025. Read on for all the details.
digest:
October was a busy month for all CIG staff, with patch launches, Pyro in the PTU, and (of course) CitizenCon 2954. Alongside these major events, progress on upcoming features continued, with many teams finalizing content for Alpha 4.0 and 2025. Read on for all the details. To note, this will be the last PU Report of the year, with November and December’s entry coming in January. We’ll see you next time!
- AI (Content): Last month, the AI Content team supported the social behaviors tied to Stanton’s derelict outposts and settlements, which will be used for new mission content.
- AI (Features): October saw AI Features improving Human combat features for Alpha 4.0.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech continued to support Server Meshing, synchronizing the Subsumption component between dedicated servers so that NPCs continue their assigned behaviors when switching.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): Throughout October, the Game Intelligence Development team polished StarScript v1.0 for its internal release.
- Animation: Last month, the Animation team worked on the valakkar and ‘space cow’ alongside adjustments to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): In October, the Character Art team focused on tasks related to CitizenCon.
- Art (Ships): October saw the Ship team complete the final content review for the RSI Polaris, while the final content tasks are currently in progress for the MISC Starlancer MAX.
- Community: The Community team began the month supporting Day of the Vara with the Pumpkin Decorating and Killer Klips from Outer Space contests.
- Economy: The Economy team continued their ongoing work on Pyro and began implementing some of the balance changes mentioned in previous Monthly Reports.
- Mission Design: In October, the Mission Design team finalized the Save Stanton quest chain.
- Narrative: The Narrative team tackled a multitude of tasks in the leadup to CitizenCon alongside ongoing work outside of the event.
- Online Technology: In October, the Online Services team progressed with features for Alpha 4.0.
- R&D: The R&D team spent the last few months supporting the introduction of dynamic weather.
- VFX: October saw the VFX team supporting various CitizenCon presentations, including those featuring new biomes, base building, and Levski.

- MISC Starlancer MAX: Building, balancing, and implementing MISC's large multi-crew cargo ship, the MISC Starlancer MAX, into the game.
- Argo CSV-SM: Building, balancing, and implementing Argo's flatbed hauling ground vehicle, the Argo CSV-SM, into the game.

- Acidic Caves: Implementing the acidic cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Rock Caves: Implementing the rock cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Additional Player Customization: Following the release of the new character customizer in Alpha 3.23, this update adds additional hair and facial hair options, as well as face piercings.
- Multi-Tool Updates: Bringing the multi-tool in line with Squadron 42, including adding additional functionality like cutting (for specific scenarios), repair, and updates like improved handling, integrated UI, and the…
- Life Support: Implementing the first iteration of onboard life support systems in ships, which entails a ship component that generates breathable gas when turned on, and management of said life support component…
- Engineering: Allows players to manage, maintain and repair various ship systems.
- Fire Hazard: Implementing the Fire Hazard system, which tracks fire & temperature on static and dynamic objects.
- Fire Extinguisher: All tasks required to implement functioning fire extinguishers in-game.
- Solar Burst: Solar Bursts are dangerous natural disasters that happen regularly around older stars like Pyro.
- Charge/Drain: Adding the ability for players to drain, store, and charge objects with power using the multi-tool.
- Transit System Refactor: Reworking the Transit System used for trams and elevators.

- Release View: The following deliverables have completed final review for Alpha 4.0, therefore we are changing their status to Committed:
- Server Meshing V1: The initial implementation of Server Meshing enables multiple servers per shard to improve load distribution and facilitates navigation between two solar systems.
- Jump Points: Implementing the first jump point into the persistent universe, connecting the Stanton and Pyro systems together.
- Pyro I: Pyro I is the first planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro II - Monox: Monox (Pyro II) is the second planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro III - Bloom: Bloom (Pyro III) is the third planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro IV: Pyro IV is the outermost moon of Pyro V, and astronomers theorize that it was once the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro V: Pyro V is the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro VI - Terminus: Terminus (Pyro VI) is the outermost world of the Pyro system.
- Ignis: Ignis is the innermost moon of the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vatra: Vatra is the second moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Adir: Adir is the third moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fairo: Fairo is the fourth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fuego: Fuego is the fifth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vuur: Vuur is the sixth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Pyro Space Stations: Adding rundown rest stop stations to the Pyro system, which provide basic services such as repair, sustenance, and commerce.
- Fauna - Quasi Grazer: These large, warm-blooded herd animals were originally discovered on the vast plains of Quasi on Terra.
- Outposts - Colonialism: A small home for AI to live and shelter.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: November & December 2024
summary: It’s the first Monthly Report of 2025! To kick off the reporting year, we’re looking back to the end of 2024, detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe in November and December. Read on for all the details behind Alpha 4.0’s development and beyond.
digest:
It’s the first Monthly Report of 2025! To kick off the reporting year, we’re looking back to the end of 2024, detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe in November and December. Read on for all the details behind Alpha 4.0’s development and beyond.
- AI (Content): The AI team ended 2024 progressing with tasks for Alpha 4.0.
- AI (Features): In November and December, the AI Feature team progressed with combat for Pyro, particularly for Alpha 4.0’s Contested Zones.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech spent the last two months making performance improvements to AI systems and progressing with new features.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): Throughout November and December, the Game Intelligence Development team continued to close down StarScript 1.1, updating the old Apollo documentation to the new UX and adding documentation to the…
- Animation: November saw the Animation team create player-interaction animations for hacking and door panels.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team supported StarWear art debt and fixed bugs for the live releases.
- Art (Ships): The Ship Art team spent the end of 2024 putting the finishing touches on upcoming vehicles that will be revealed or released this year.
- Community: The Community team began the busy months of November and December with a recap of CitizenCon 2954 and by making all presentations from the event available on YouTube.
- Core Gameplay: All Core Gameplay teams were heavily involved in addressing stability and performance issues found during Alpha 4.0 PTU.
- Economy: The end of 2024 saw the Economy team adjust the prices of quantum and hydrogen fuel to account for new tank sizes.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: For the graphics department, the end of 2024 largely involved making significant performance and stability improvements to Alpha 4.0.
- Interactables: Interactables developed assets for Contested Zones, such as keycards, server blades, and fuse slots, and completed a performance and bug pass.
- Locations: The Locations team spent the end of 2024 supporting the Alpha 4.0 build, including polishing, optimizing, and bug-fixing Pyro’s Contested Zones and outposts.
- Mission Design: The ongoing mission refactor continued, with bugs being prioritized and triaged.
- Narrative: Over the past two months, the Narrative team focused on finishing mission content text for Alpha 4.0.
- Online Technology: In November and December, Online Services finalized the backend services crucial to several key features, including the mission-system refactor, the entity-subscription service/marker refactor, the…
- R&D: In November and December, the R&D team continued to finalize the core system components for the first version of dynamic weather.
- Tech Art/Animation: The Technical Animation team continued with a range of long-term tasks to facilitate improvements across the board.
- Tech Design: Throughout November and December, Tech Design primarily focused on the Contested Zones.
- VFX: In November, VFX supported the Vehicle teams with the Mirai Guardian and the Locations teams with a variety of Pyro location work.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: January 2025
summary: Welcome to January’s PU Monthly Report! Hot on the heels of the recent November/December report, we’re back detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe at the beginning of 2025.
digest:
Welcome to January’s PU Monthly Report! Hot on the heels of the recent November/December report, we’re back detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe at the beginning of 2025. Read on for all the latest updates on AI, core gameplay, missions, narrative, and much more.
- AI (Content): The AI Content team began the year prototyping an upcoming NPC that will utilize an amalgamation of several behavior types.
- AI (Features): In January, AI Feature’s primary focus was split between bug fixes and creature-behavior improvements.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): The Game Intelligence Development (GID) team continued their work on StarScript, with January’s goal being the implementation of the ‘views’ feature.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech began the year fixing bugs, improving features, and kicking off new tech.
- Animation: The Gameplay Animation team began the year working on the kopion hound and various sizes of the valakkar.
- Art (Characters): In January, the Character team continued working on StarWear art debt.
- Community: The Community team kicked off the year by announcing the winners of the Gift that Keeps on Giving video contest.
- Core Gameplay: Throughout January, the Core Gameplay teams investigated and improved many issues found during Alpha 4.0 Live Preview.
- Economy: The Economy team kicked off the year gathering feedback and data regarding the changes they implemented in Alpha 4.0.
- Mission Design: Mission Design spent time fixing bugs for Fight For Pyro, ensuring it was ready for release.
- Narrative: The Narrative team began 2025 meeting with multiple disciplines to solidify new ways of delivering in-game narrative content.
- Online Technology: In January, the Live Tools team released a new major feature to manage access and permissions in a more granular and versatile way.
- R&D: The R&D team began January investigating rare PU crashes inside the planet-spawning code.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.0.1, the VFX team worked on the MISC Fortune and elements of another vehicle, which will be shared soon.

summary: Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the latest updates from the developers working on the Persistent Universe, including the AI, Core Gameplay, Narrative, Missions, Tech Design, and UI teams.
digest:
Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the latest updates from the developers working on the Persistent Universe, including the AI, Core Gameplay, Narrative, Missions, Tech Design, and UI teams.
- AI (Content): AI Content continued updating the broken air traffic controller behavior throughout the main landing zones, with fixes entering the QATR process for validation, stress testing, and to ensure they…
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features improved and polished creature behaviors.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In February, the Game Intelligence Development team continued to fix StarScript crashes reported by the designers and QA testers.
- AI (Tech): Last month, the AI Tech team progressed with work that will allow them to voxelize huge areas for 3D navigation.
- Animation: Animation progressed for creatures such as new movement for the kopion to give it more ability to traverse its environment.
- Art (Characters): In February, the Character team kicked off a new creature, continued to work through StarWear art debt, and progressed with two new stealth armors.
- Community: In early February, the Community team resumed their regular updates to the Roadmap, This Week in Star Citizen, and the Arena Commander Schedule, alongside general support for upcoming patches…
- Core Gameplay: In February, the Core Gameplay team (one of the primary drivers behind the stability and quality-of-life initiative) continued fixing numerous bugs.
- Mission Design: Mission Design focused on updating some old missions that weren’t included in the recent refactor.
- Narrative: A major highlight for Narrative in February was the recent performance-capture shoot focused on adding new narratives and characters.
- Online Technology: The Online Technology team began the year making tweaks and fixes to enable more in-game items to persist long-term.
- R&D: In February, work on the new method for large-scale soft-terrain shadow generation continued.
- Tech Design: In February, Tech Design worked closely with Mission Design on upcoming content releases that players will hear more about in the future.
- UI: February saw the UI team focus on bug fixing, user experience, and vehicles.
- VFX: VFX spent part of February prepping for content releasing later this year.

title: Roadmap Roundup - February 26, 2025
summary: With the Roadmap just updated, here is a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes.
digest:
As we emphasized in the last Letter from the Chairman and throughout our messaging this year, our top priority for 2025 is improving playability. A key part of this effort is refining how we manage feature development—with features now being developed in a separate branch and only migrating over when they are ready.
- Release View: Deliverables released with 4.0.0 and 4.0.1 were marked as Released.
- Additions to the Star Citizen 1.0 column:: Improving atmospheric flight dynamics with functional control surfaces, allowing for more precise maneuvering and realistic aerodynamics.
- Progress Tracker: You can now find a preview of many of the things that we are currently actively working on in the Progress Tracker, with more additions to come at a later time.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: March 2025
summary: This month’s PU Report features progress on a variety of ongoing development initiatives, including the recently released Alpha 4.1, upcoming vehicles, AI work, and mission content. Read on for the latest updates!
digest:
This month’s PU Report features progress on a variety of ongoing development initiatives, including the recently released Alpha 4.1, upcoming vehicles, AI work, and mission content. Read on for the latest updates!
- AI (Content): For the recent debut of Star Citizen’s first alien NPC, Wikelo, AI Content worked alongside the Narrative Design, Design, Animation, Audio, and Character Art teams to prototype the character’s…
- AI (Features): In March, AI Feature’s priority was the valakkar, specifically the juvenile variant.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In March, Game Intelligence Development had two main focuses: the full implementation of Views and organization and analysis for Mission System 2.0.
- AI (Tech): Last month, AI Tech continued to work on features that will improve overall detail and quality, including finalizing work for the spatial priority solver and priority beacon system.
- Animation: The Animation team continued developing various sizes of valakkar alongside making updates to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): In March, the Character Art team continued to work on a new creature for the PU alongside StarWear art debt.
- Art (Ships): In March, the UK-based Vehicle Content team completed the Drake Golem mining ship and Argo ATLS GEO mining power suit.
- Community: The Community team kicked off March with support for Stella Fortuna, launching the Bar Crawl screenshot contest and publishing a catch-all post highlighting the exciting activities available to…
- Core Gameplay: For the Argo ATLS GEO, the Core Gameplay team completed the suit’s mining and thruster functionality, added a health bar and damage states, and supported additional improvements to the base ATLS.
- Economy: The Economy team provided balancing support for Supply or Die, with the devs deeming it over-tuned on release.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: Last month, the Graphics team overhauled GPU memory management.
- Mission Design: March saw Mission Design continuing to fix up various older missions that were deprioritized in the refactor.
- Narrative: Aligning with the increased release schedule cadence, Alpha 4.1 was a major focus for the Narrative team in March.
- Online Technology: In March, the Live Tools team focused on improving the usability of their main support tool, Hex.
- R&D: In March, gas cloud detail rendering was improved using techniques used by planetary volumetric clouds.
- Tech Design: Tech Design spent March working on an upcoming in-game event, supporting Mission Design with gameplay entity and logic flow setup.
- VFX: VFX progressed with their tasks for the valakkar.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: April 2025
summary: Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! With the UEEN Invictus fleet currently preparing to make the jump to Stanton, most teams touched on the upcoming festivities throughout the month. However, a lot of work was also done toward features and content coming later this year – read on for more de
digest:
Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! With the UEEN Invictus fleet currently preparing to make the jump to Stanton, most teams touched on the upcoming festivities throughout the month. However, a lot of work was also done toward features and content coming later this year - read on for more details.
- AI (Content): AI Content spent the majority of April preparing the release of Alpha 4.1.1, including the communications that players can now receive from mission givers.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features focused on refining the juvenile valakkar.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In April, the Game Intelligence Development (GID) team worked on various StarScript improvements, including allowing users to ‘right click’ task-extension links and search for an existing task to…
- AI (Tech): AI Tech progressed with the pathfinder system, making various improvements and cleaning up requests involving multiple start and end locations.
- Animation: Last month, the Animation team continued to support the studio-wide initiative of focusing on content for the PU.
- Art (Ships): In the EU, the team focused on closing out tasks for Invictus Launch Week, including three new ships planned for release at the event.
- Community: The Community team began April supporting Triggerfish, including the parody patch notes for the scaled-down EZ Hab Arena Commander Map.
- Core Gameplay: Several of the Core Gameplay teams spent the month stabilizing and improving the new space-themed missions in Alpha 4.1.1.
- Economy: Last month, the Economy team were involved in the new content coming in Alpha 4.1.1, including items and vehicles for Invictus.
- Mission Design: With most of their recent fundamental tech work complete, the team focused on improving mission quality.
- Narrative: In April, the Narrative team’s main focus was on a suite of new missions and support for Invictus Launch Week.
- Online Technology: In April, the Live Tools team worked on various features, including new sanction types and improvements to scheduling global system messages.
- R&D: In April, various improvements were made to the lightning evaluation that's part of the cloud and atmosphere raymarch.
- UI: Last month, the UI team worked to implement unique UI styles for several upcoming vehicles.
- VFX: Last month, VFX worked toward completing their tasks on vehicles and weapons for Invictus Launch Week.

Alongside patch fixes and other various changes, many teams touched on tech, locations, and updates coming later this year. Read on for all the latest info.
- AI Content: AI Content continued to support Star Citizen’s monthly release cadence.
- AI (Features): In May, AI Features ensured Human combat is in an optimal state in several key areas: ammo management and behavior, cover usage, first reactions and perception, attack and defend areas…

- Art (Ships): As usual, May was extremely busy for the Vehicle Content teams as they supported new releases, progressed with upcoming vehicles, and kicked off projects for the next year or so.
- Community: The Community team spent much of May breaking down Community feedback/sentiment across all platforms and ensuring its delivery to the right teams internally.
- Core Gameplay: Core Gameplay are currently working through a long list of weapon improvements to further modernize the FPS experience for both Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, including tweaking how disruptive weapon…
- Lighting: Lighting supported all recent and upcoming patch releases, including adding environmental and dynamic lighting to interactable event locations in Pyro.
- Locations: The Locations teams continued to support the ongoing monthly content releases.
- Narrative: May brought with it a flurry of activity for the Narrative team.
- Online Technology: In May, the Network team continued work on Dynamic Server Meshing, separating the DGS assignment from the territory manager.
- UI: In May, the team completed the UI for an upcoming event, creating various screens to support the narrative and gameplay.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: June 2025
summary: June was a busy month at CIG, with most teams making final updates toward Alpha 4.2 and upcoming content. Read on for all the details of last month’s development, including the latest from the Ships, AI Tech, and Core Gameplay teams.
digest:
June was a busy month at CIG, with most teams making final updates toward Alpha 4.2 and upcoming content. Read on for all the details of last month’s development, including the latest from the Ships, AI Tech, and Core Gameplay teams.
- AI Content: June saw AI Content meeting with the directors and Combat AI team to keep pushing the development of the updated combatant wildline script.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features completed their tasks for the irradiated valakkar, which made its debut in the PU.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): The Game Intelligence Development team started the month with meetings relating to StarScript, Mission System 2.0, the commentator model, the density profiler, entity scripting, Mannequin, and the…
- AI (Tech): Throughout June, the AI tech team provided bug fixes and support for the Alpha 4.2 release, including optimizing how navigation-mesh regeneration accounts for navigation links.
- Animation: Animation spent the month supporting the irradiated valakkar alongside another new creature for later this year.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Anvil Paladin continued through greybox, with additional artists being moved onto it as their other tasks were completed to help prepare for its July gate review.
- Community: June began with a celebration of diversity and culture as the team launched Show Us Your Colors 2025.
- Core Gameplay: With the new Storm Breaker content, the Core Gameplay teams added several updates to radiation, hazard areas, and damage-over-time handling.
- Mission Design: Last month, Mission Design worked to close out the Storm Breaker sandbox activity for release.
- Narrative: Following Alpha 4.2’s release, the Narrative team focused on the next two upcoming patches, which will feature a variety of new missions.
- Online Technology: The Online Services team continued to work on the ‘item imprint system’- design aspects are being discussed, technical documentation is being written, and service development began.
- R&D: Gas cloud rendering was further refined based on the improvements implemented in March.
- VFX: The VFX Code and Art teams worked on several things for Alpha 4.2.

digest:
With last month’s patch launching and a new one fast approaching, no Star Citizen dev has been short of things to do. Read on for all the latest development updates from each team, including AI, Ships, Core Gameplay, Narrative, and VFX.
- AI Content: July saw the AI Content team continue the ongoing initiatives mentioned in recent Monthly Reports, including the push on new combatant wildline sets, which will be completed following some…
- AI (Features): In July, the AI Features team continued to develop new creatures, including prototype gameplay for a boss fight.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In July, the Game Intelligence Development team continued to work on the prototype for Mission System v2.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech began the month improving navigation.
- Animation: Last month, the team progressed with a new ship enter/exit template animation alongside pickups for bespoke gameplay features for an upcoming PU release.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art spent the month creating new armors and armor variants.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Anvil Paladin had its greybox gate review.
- Community: Much of July was spent on ensuring player feedback was landing in front of the relevant developers/teams, alongside ongoing planning and support for the upcoming CitizenCon Direct.
- Core Gameplay: Throughout July, the Core Gameplay teams focused on freight elevators, providing fixes for critical issues raised during the Resource Drive event while also improving the debugging tools alongside…
- Economy: The Economy team is currently analyzing their recent community poll.
- Mission Design: The Mission Design team monitored the Resource Drive event to see how players interacted with the event, fixed small exploits, and helped Engineering fix the mission-generation system.
- Narrative: Last month, the Narrative team were deeply involved in getting the upcoming Alpha 4.3 patch ready for release by refining and tweaking mission text, objectives, UI screens, and branding to deliver a…
- Online Technology: Live Tools improved how developers report bugs through the crash handler, making it more reliable.
- R&D: In July, the R&D team’s focus shifted exclusively to analyzing performance and optimizing engine and game code.
- UI: The UI team continued to support an upcoming gameplay event, contributing more interactive and environmental screens than ever before.
- VFX: VFX’s main focus throughout July was Alpha 4.3, including new locations, bespoke events, vehicles, and weapons.

digest:
From Ship Showdown 2955 to Alpha 4.3: Dark Territory, August was packed with action and adventure. Read on for all the details on what was done to finalize last month’s content alongside ongoing progress on the wealth of new vehicles, locations, missions, and features coming in the near and not-so-near future.
- AI Content: AI Content continued to progress with several ongoing initiatives, including refactoring one of the NPC archetypes important to landing-zone infrastructure.
- AI (Features): The AI Features team began the month by improving NPC weapon overheating, a feature initially developed for Squadron 42.
- AI (Tech): The AI Tech team progressed with cross-navigation volume pathfinding.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In August, the Game Intelligence Development team continued to work on the density profiler, developing new IMGUI control.
- Animation: Throughout August, Animation worked on improvements to the kopion as well as a new creature.
- Art (Characters): Last month, the Character Art team progressed with armor for a new gang and supported requests for subscriber flair items and CitizenCon Direct.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, three unannounced ships progressed throughout August.
- Community: Throughout August, the Community team continued to capture community sentiment, track feedback, and relay it to development teams, ensuring that player input continues to inform future updates.
- Core Gameplay: Throughout August, the Core Gameplay teams were heavily involved in the Alpha 4.3 release, though they also made significant progress across many large gameplay systems.
- Economy: Last month, the Economy team progressed with the new iteration of the economy based on data they recently gathered.
- Mission Design: The Mission team worked hard toward the release of Alpha 4.3, including the new ASD Onyx facilities.
- Narrative: With the release of ASD’s Onyx facilities, the Narrative team turned their focus to polishing the next round of content that players will discover there.
- Online Technology: In August, the Online Services team collaborated with QA to test the stow-context API.
- R&D: In August, the R&D team’s focus remained on analyzing performance and optimizing engine and game code.
- VFX: Multiple locations, props, and gameplay elements integral to the entire Alpha 4.3/4.3.1 flow required VFX support, which resulted in incredible visuals that the community have already given great…

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: September 2025
summary: With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue’s Descent live and another action-packed update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.
digest:
With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue's Descent live and another thrilling update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September in pursuit of this new content, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.
- AI Content: The AI Content team continued to test updates to some of the landing-zone NPCs, looping in the QA team to help stress test the setup to ensure it can take the strain of extensive use and trigger any…
- AI (Features): AI Features updated numerous features last month, beginning with AIWeaponComponent, which will now remain in sync with weapon statuses, allowing them to work better in unison.
- AI (Tech): September saw AI Tech improve NPCs using elevators by simplifying the set up of the transit carriage.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In September, the Game Intelligence Development team focused on completing the next milestone for Mission System 2.0.
- Animation: The Animation team continued to work on an upcoming creature and ‘boss’ fight alongside supporting a new mission giver.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team finalized both new armors and a new gang.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, work continued to bring the RSI Aurora and Aegis Hammerhead up to modern standard.
- Community: The team kicked off the month with the grand finale of this year’s Ship Showdown, where the RSI Polaris claimed the crown.
- Core Gameplay: As part of ongoing medical gameplay improvements, the team provided support for bespoke ‘take’ and ‘place’ animations, and reworked the implementation of players clearing their respawn point in…
- Economy: The Economy team began the month exploring how to make the players’ impact on freelancing commodity trading more impactful and longer lasting.
- Mission Design: Mission Design began September finalizing the last narrative mission for the ASD facilities before looking forward to the rest of the year’s content.
- Narrative: In September, the Narrative team focused on tasks to help close out the rest of the year strongly.
- Online Technology: Last month, the Live Tools team updated the error reporting pipeline, including moving panic migration from Heap to Laravel.
- R&D: In September, the R&D team’s focus remained exclusively on analyzing performance and optimizing engine and game code.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.3.2, VFX finished up their tasks for the ASD locations and final event work, while the RSI Apollo Triage and Medivac received their VFX passes.

title: Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy: Nyx
summary: Welcome to another edition of Traveler’s Guide to the Galaxy. These dispatches aim to provide early insights into the lore and design shaping new locations coming to the Star Citizen universe. This time, we venture to Nyx, the third star system to join the ‘verse, coming in Alpha 4.4.
digest:
- Star System: Welcome to another edition of Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy.
- WELCOME TO THE NYX SYSTEM: Nyx is an unclaimed planetary system situated at the border of a dark nebula.
- Settlement: The system's primary settlement, Levski, is built into a large asteroid within the Glaciem Ring.
- THE TANAKA MEMORIAL: The entrance of Levski is dominated by a statue of an unnamed worker holding the lifeless body of Anthony Tanaka, a child laborer who was executed by an Advocacy agent in 2757 for refusing to…
- STRONGER TOGETHER: A faction originally formed by people fleeing the unjust Messer regime, they founded a utopian colony in a ready-made station on an asteroid in the Nyx system.
- NOTABLY NYX'S: Remote, rugged, and rich in character, Delamar has quietly become a source of some of the most distinctive drinks in the UEE.
- TRISE SLING: While Trise Cordial isn't native to Nyx, its most famous cocktail may well be.
- JYNX GIN: Distilled and bottled on Delamar, Jynx Gin owes its striking coloration and part of its mystique to the omphalotus mushroom.
- Beyond Alpha 4.4: What follows is a preview of content that's planned for future updates and not included in Alpha 4.4.
- LOCATIONS: New locations will arrive with future content drops.
- NYX I: A green yet uninhabitable world undergoing an experimental terraformation process, Nyx I may soon have an atmosphere that will let everyone breathe free.
- NYX II: The air on Nyx II is sweltering, stifling, and extremely poisonous.
- NYX III: Furthest planet from the star at the center of the Nyx system, Nyx III is an ice giant with a stormy atmosphere.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: October 2025
summary: Welcome to the latest PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the behind-the-scenes details of development throughout October, including progress on Nyx, upcoming ships, AI behaviors, the in-game economy, and more.
digest:
Welcome to the latest PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the behind-the-scenes details of development throughout October, including progress on Nyx, upcoming ships, AI behaviors, the in-game economy, and more.
- AI Content: In October, the Narrative and Social AI teams supported several initiatives for the upcoming Alpha 4.4 patch, including landing zone fixes.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features continued to iterate on first reaction and usable animations.
- AI (Tech): The AI Team made improvements to navigation-mesh generation, including to the generation algorithm.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In October 2025, the Game Intelligence Development team worked toward the next milestone for Mission System v2, focusing on implementing ‘outline properties’, the first pass of a prototype property…
- Animation: Animation worked on the Yormandi throughout October alongside improvements to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team finalized various armors for a new gang and in-game rewards, and progressed with a new heavy armor and clothing items.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team supported the release of the Anvil Paladin, Esperia Stinger, and Grey’s Market Shiv at CitizenCon Direct.
- Community: October began with the return of Day of the Vara, the ‘verse’s spirited fall event, which the Community team supported with an informative thread and a pair of creepy contests.
- Core Gameplay: The Core Gameplay teams pushed forward on the inventory revamp.
- Economy: The team spent last month building the economy of Nyx and giving the system character.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: Folllowing the Preview Channel testing of Vulkan, the graphics team fixed many performance issues, the vast majority of which were caused by running out of video memory.
- Mission Design: Mission Design worked on the recent limited-time event, the Frontier Fighters Finale.
- Narrative: Last month, the Narrative team focused on the final preparations for the release of Nyx.
- Online Technology: October saw the Online Services team progress with Item Recovery T1 and the early stages of instancing.
- R&D: In October, the R&D team worked on engine optimizations that will eventually make their way into the PU.
- VFX: VFX supported all of the game’s upcoming vehicles, with some standouts being the Shiv and Stinger.

title: IAE 2955 MISC
summary: Legendary shipbuilder with a focus on heavy industry.
digest: The backbone of the Empire, MISC ships carry the bulk of Humanity’s vital supplies to wherever they’re needed. Although prolific in hauling, MISC’s expertise runs deep, with a wide range of accomplished industry and personal vehicles honed by decades of serving the UEE.

title: IAE 2955 Mirai
summary: Fast, light, and laser-focused on performance.
digest: Now well-established following its breakaway from MISC, Mirai is known solely for performance. Be it the record-breaking Razor, the frenetic Fury, or the heavy-hitting Guardian, every Mirai ship is honed for speed, agility, and responsiveness.

title: IAE 2955 Kruger Intergalactic
summary: Bringing high-performance spacecraft with classic styling.
digest: Although famed for its category-defining snub craft, Kruger has recently turned its deep manufacturing knowhow toward the Light Fighter market. The result is the Wolf, a series of gorgeous ships with unique weapon loadouts.

title: Kruger L-22 Alpha Wolf - The Next Fight
summary: Modified and customizable for your desired offense in combat, the L-22 Alpha Wolf flies with agility and striking elegance, just like its predecessor, but with a new laser-driven style.
digest:
- THE FUTURE IS YOURS: Kruger swiftly returns following the stylish debut of its aesthetic masterpiece, the L-21 Wolf, with an altered variant.
- LASER PRECISION: In addition to an augmented missile load, the L-22 Alpha Wolf is armed with retractable laser repeaters for a new and brutal combat experience.
- EMBRACE MODIFICATION: Kruger does what it does best, with modifiable parts for the L-22 Alpha Wolf and its predecessor, the L-21 Wolf.

title: Behind the Ships - Kruger L-22 Alpha Wolf
digest: A is for aggression. A is for aesthetic. A is for Alpha. Kruger sweeps by for another attack run with a new variant, versatile weapons kits, and a new winglet makeover. Just when you thought this thing couldn’t get any sexier.

digest: IAE expands its showcase this year to include the offsite presentation of Grey's Market, a smaller ship shop that produces top-tier vehicles from an amalgamation of recovered high-end parts and components.

title: IAE 2955 Gatac Manufacture
summary: Wild cargo haulers from the Xi’an themselves.
digest: Gatac takes genuine alien cargo ships and adopts them for Human use, all while maintaining their beautiful organic design. Despite their appearance, these haulers are some of the most capable in the galaxy, as proven by centuries of Xi’an use.

title: IAE 2955 Esperia
summary: Accurate replicas of historic Tevarin and Vanduul spacecraft.
digest: Esperia recreates ships lost to time and space. It’s the only shipbuilder to offer accurate replicas of contemporary Vanduul fighters, the likes of which are currently terrorizing Human colonies in the outer reaches of the Empire. Get up close and personal with the enemy at IAE.

digest: Banu shipbuilding is a deeply involved process spanning years of iteration and refinement. However, when a vehicle finally makes it to market, it’s refined and true to purpose. See the Defender, one of the most single-minded fighters at IAE 2955.

title: IAE 2955 Aopoa
summary: Genuine alien fighters, adapted for Human use.
digest: The combat arm of Xi’an shipbuilding, Aopoa’s alien fighters look and fly like nothing else. Heavy hitting and exceptionally agile, they take a skilled pilot to fly, but the results often make up for the risks.

title: IAE 2955 Drake Interplanetary
summary: Drake’s back to say you CAN go it alone in the ‘verse!
digest: The outsider’s choice. Loved for its rough-and-ready build quality, Drake does the job without bells and whistles, be it combat, mining, hauling, or other less-legal pursuits. Plus, don’t miss two new releases shaking up their respective markets this IAE. Here we go again, folks. Drake has descended onto the show floor, bringing all the grit, gumption, and gall that its fans can muster. Join Lexxy and Gale as they debate variant value, generalist gear, and Drake’s salty-yet-unsavory past. Not forgetting, the return of a special guest for an... er, unexpected turn of events.

- Sizable Storage: The only hauler of its size with 2x 32 SCU cargo capacity, the Golem OX helps you make your living, 64 SCUs at a time.
- A Solo Operation: This self-reliant slogger needs only you to bring home the credits.
- Deployable Tractor Beam: Load and unload your external haul remotely with a rear tractor beam, the perfect way to save on your most precious resource, your time.

title: Engineering Gameplay Guide
summary: A starter guide to developing Engineering gameplay.
digest:
- Engineering Gameplay Guide: A key pillar of Star Citizen’s vehicle gameplay loop is Engineering.
- WHAT IS ENGINEERING GAMEPLAY?: Engineering gameplay revolves around managing resources across your ships and vehicles through the Resource Network.
- TOOLS: All engineers need to consider the following necessary tools to perform their tasks:
- ENGINEERING ITEMS: These are the elements found within vehicles that will support the Engineering gameplay loop:
- Components: Core elements that drive the main functionality of major vehicle systems.
- Relays: Link systems together and allow resources to travel through the ship.
- MFD Power and Diagnostic: Provide a high level overview of power distribution and resource management.
- Engineering Console: The beating heart of Engineering in most ships with interiors, giving crew the tools to review power flow, allocate resources, control systems, and understand the ship’s overall state.
- WHAT ARE COMPONENTS?: Components provide the main functionality for all major vehicle systems; they are the core organs that keep the ship flying.
- ENGINEERING RESOURCES: Engineering gameplay is the physical expression of the Resource Network and the management that surrounds it.
- POWER DISTRIBUTION: Distributing power throughout your vehicle is one of the most important responsibilities for any engineer.
- ENGINEERING CONSOLE: The Engineering console is the central hub for monitoring and controlling system performance across the ship.
- COMPONENTS DETAILS: All components are linked through relays, allowing resources to move throughout your ship.
- LIFE SUPPORT THROUGH THE SHIP: Engineers must ensure that Life Support is always active throughout the ship to maintain a breathable atmosphere.
- ARMOR: In Alpha 4.5, ships gain Armor as an extra layer of defense.
- DAMAGE PENETRATION: Different weapon types perform better or worse against armor, creating opportunities to target internal systems more effectively.
- WEAR AND TEAR (Full System Coming Soon): Over time, if components are not properly maintained, they will suffer wear and tear that reduces their effectiveness.
- HEAT AND FIRE: Heat is now a crucial element for pilots and engineers to monitor.
- MALFUNCTIONS: Components that are damaged, worn, or running too hot can begin to malfunction, and the results can range from reduced performance, to complete shutdowns.
- CRITICAL FAILURE: Critical failures are catastrophic states that may cause your entire vehicle to explode.
- REPAIRING: Repair gameplay is essential to extending the life of all components and your vehicle as a whole.
- ENGINEERING AVAILABILITY IN ALL VEHICLES: As of Alpha 4.8, every single vehicle in Star Citizen is Engineering-enabled and capable of the baseline experience.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: February 2026
summary: Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! There’s a huge amount of content coming to ’verse in the next few weeks, including new and returning missions, the latest ships from RSI, and thrilling activities and locations around Nyx. Read on for everything done toward this exciting upcoming release.
digest:
Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! There’s a huge amount of content coming to ‘verse in the next few weeks, including new and returning missions, the latest ships from RSI, and thrilling activities and locations around Nyx. Read on for everything done toward this exciting upcoming release.
- AI Content: The Social AI team began the month bug fixing in support of Alpha 4.6 before looking to future releases.
- AI (Features & Tech): Last month, AI Features & Tech improved underground traversal for the valakkar, prototyping its future speeds.
- Animation: Animation spent February improving assets for the kopion, while Facial Animation focused on the first performance-capture shoot of the year.
- Art (Characters): February saw Character Art polishing assets for Alpha 4.7 alongside working through art debt in preparation for StarWear.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team completed the art phases for the Aegis Hammerhead gold standard, with the ship moving to downstream teams for close-out.
- Community: The Community team began the month by publishing the January PU Monthly Report and preparing for February’s seasonal and community-driven events.
- Core Gameplay: As seen by Evocati players during recent Tech Previews, the Core Gameplay team made solid progress on the Inventory Rework.
- Economy: The Economy team spent part of February tracking exploits, in particular those that resulted in item duplication or large quantities of aUEC being generated.
- Mission Design: In February, the devs continued to work on the Alpha 4.7 mission pack, which adds more content to Nyx and revives the courier missions that have been waiting for a refactor since Alpha 4.0.
- Narrative: In February, the Narrative team focused their efforts on Alpha 4.7, which will expand the content available in Nyx.
- Online Technology: In February, the Network team focused on improving stability and reliability across Hybrid/DGS, resolving several high‑impact crashes, watchdog timeouts, and replication errors.
- R&D: In February, work on the improved ground fog continued; a dissipation model was implemented to simulate fog behavior during a full day/night cycle.
- VFX: In February, the VFX team focused heavily on supporting Alpha 4.7, contributing to the development of new locations, creatures, props, and vehicles as additional deliverables for Nyx came online.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: March 2026
summary: Welcome to March’s Monthly Report. As usual, there was a huge amount of work going on across CIG’s global studios, from the final touches of Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock to exciting content coming soon and later in the year. Read on for all the details!
digest:
Welcome to March’s Monthly Report. As usual, there was a huge amount of work going on across CIG’s global studios, from the final touches of Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock to exciting content coming soon and later in the year. Read on for all the details!
- AI Content: Last month saw AI make numerous fixes while continuing to build for the future.
- AI (Features & Tech): For Alpha 4.7, AI Features & Tech solved issues caused by inclusions after breaching and looked into various bugs.
- Animation: March saw the Animation team working on snake and worm-type enemies, including creating new behavior animations.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team progressed with projects for Alpha 4.8 alongside in-game assets.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team progressed with the Gatac Railen, preparing it for its greybox gate review at the end of March.
- Audio: Last month, the Audio team successfully delivered their work for Alpha 4.7.
- Community: The Community team kicked off March by publishing the February PU Monthly Report and laying the groundwork for an eventful month ahead.
- Core Gameplay: The Core Gameplay team spent part of March progressing hacking, with the devs polishing items, improving the tutorial, and ensuring the UI is always correctly aligned to the player.
- Creature Content: March saw the formation of a new team, Creature Content, to focus on the ongoing development of ‘Star Paws’ features.
- Economy: March saw the Economy team moving onto features for Alpha 4.8, which will bring new item crafting, commodity trading, and item recovery systems to the ‘verse.
- Game Intelligence Development: In March 2026, the Game Intelligence Development team primarily focused on the ongoing design and planning work for Mission System v2.
- Level Design (UK & DE): While March saw the Level Design teams progressing on a variety of locations, the primary focus was on Nyx’s social stations and QV Breaker Station locations, which went live in Alpha 4.7.
- Mission Design: Mission Design completed the second Nyx mission pack, which expands the amount of content for players, including moving some factions to utilize a reputation scope.
- Narrative: In March, the Narrative team continued tasks for a whole host of upcoming gameplay operations and missions.
- Online Technology: In March 2026, the Network team focused heavily on advancing the foundation for Server Meshing.
- R&D: In March, the ongoing ground-fog work continued.
- Tech Art/Animation: Over the past month, the Technical Animation team progressed with characters, creatures, interactables, cloth simulation, and the pipeline tools that support all of the above.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.7, VFX focused on finishing Nyx’s QV Breaker Station locations, such as the laser room and spacescaping, and hero moments, like the laser and asteroid interior.

summary: Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! digest:
Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! With Alpha 4.7 well established in the ’verse and the recent point patch adding new delivery missions around Nyx, most of the devs used the last month to progress with features, content, and other deliverables coming next. Read on for everything that happened behind the scenes of the PU throughout April.
- AI Content: April saw the Narrative Design team introduce Tactical Strike Groups.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Tech & Features began April with various optimization tasks, including a refactor of the Hermite cubic spline implementation to achieve better performance.
- Animation: Animation progressed with an upcoming creature, adding new actions and attacks alongside improving existing data.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team spent April developing a new armor set and in-game rewards.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team progressed with the Drake Ironclad and Ironclad Assault.
- Art (Weapons): Last month, the Weapons team put the finishing touches on the new Kastak Arms plasma grenade, preparing it for release.
- Community: The Community team kicked April off with the publication of the March PU Monthly Report and early prep work for the Captains of Industry event.
- Core Gameplay: In April, Core Gameplay supported various initiatives and focused on bug fixing for Alpha 4.8.
- Mission Design: April saw the Mission team design fundamental changes to the contract system.
- Narrative: Narrative began April by wrapping up content for Alpha 4.8.
- Online Technology: In Montreal, the Live Tools team completed various improvements to the internal tools that keep Star Citizen's operations and development running smoothly.
- R&D: In April, further changes were made to the shader compile server to significantly improve robustness, latency, and throughput.
- Tech Art/Animation: Throughout April, the Technical Animation team continued to advance content across characters, creatures, armor, and the underlying pipeline.
- VFX: VFX worked through major tasks for Alpha 4.8, such as vehicles, including the Drake Ironclad, Tactical Strike Groups, and the Kastak Arms plasma grenade and UltiFlex Novia crossbow.

title: Gatac Tyilui - Transcend the Ordinary
summary: Gatac reveals its first carrier, with distinctive Xi’an design and spectacular zero-gravity technology.
digest:
Float, spin, and wind through this powerfully unique product of alien invention. Xi’an technology elevates the way a crew operates, the way space is utilized, and how a ship’s purpose evolves. A spectacular original, the Tyilui is not only the first alien-designed carrier on the market, but the first ship with a zero-gravity hangar, allowing for an aerial ballet of weightless operation.
- Zero Gravity: Walk on walls of alien rock, where up is down and down is wherever you need to go.
- Snub Transport: Up to four snub fighters nestle around the multi-directional zero-gravity hangar, while a capable weapons loadout protects their run to the front lines.
- Extraordinary Interior: A composition as unique as its functionality, the spacious inner chambers heighten the tranquil Xi’an aesthetic with organic material, living plants, and flowing water.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: August 2026
summary: Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
digest:
Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
- AI Content: The recent Alpha 4.10 patch marked an exciting milestone for AI Content, with the re-release of Recco Battaglia and the introduction of a narrative-driven mission chain.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Features and Tech spent August improving Starchitect, fixing nav-meshes, and progressing with Star Paws.
- Animation: Last month, animations were worked on for the apex valakkar, including for major attacks on ship targets.
- Art (Characters): In August, the Character Art team finalized a new combat armor set and its variants, completed Subscriber flair items, and progressed with a new type of armor.
- Art (Ships): The UK team began the month with a final polish pass on the Kruger Stingray after utilizing the PTU to catch a number of small bugs before its full release.
- Community: August began with the team supporting two ongoing events that started in July: Foundation Festival, which welcomes new pilots and celebrates the community members who help them find their way, and…
- Narrative: Work continued in August on generating mission text for the huge number of missions that will be arriving with Nyx I.
- Online Technology: Last month, the Online Services team focused on improving the reliability of missions and contracts, specifically the system that generates jobs and delivery tasks.
- R&D: August saw the R&D team working on planet atmosphere, including making improvements to the overcast skylight.
- Tech Art/Animation: Throughout August, the Technical Animation team focused on the systems that make characters look and move convincingly, including faces, deformation, cloth, and creatures.

title: Q&A: Aegis Sabre Raven EX and Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma
summary: We asked the Vehicle team a few questions about the two vehicles releasing with Alpha 4.10.1: Orison Relief Support. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves.
digest: Aegis Sabre Raven EX & Argo ATLS IKTI Akuma We asked the Vehicle team a few questions about the two vehicles releasing with Alpha 4.10.1: Orison Relief Support. Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves. What is a "Quantum Dampener" and how is it different than a "Quantum Snare? These are two related technologies. A Quantum Dampener (QDMP) prevents ships within range from entering quantum travel. This is useful for keeping your target from escaping the fight. A Quantum Snare can force ships out of quantum travel.
